page: Amazon Web Services x8g.2xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized virtual machine powered by AWS Neoverse-V2 Graviton processors running at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The configuration features 8 dedicated physical cores with 8 vCPUs (1 thread per core), supported by 64 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. System memory is provisioned at 128.0 GB, establishing a high memory allocation of 16.0 GB per core. The server does not bundle local disk storage and connects with a 4 Gbps baseline network speed without dedicated hardware accelerators.

In synthetic and application benchmarks, the instance demonstrates exceptional memory subsystem throughput, led by a PassMark memory score of 3,139.44 that places in the top 10% tier. Small-block cached read memory bandwidth reaches 924.86 GB/s, while large-block read and write bandwidth register at 154.74 GB/s and 77.0 GB/s respectively. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 14.47 GB/s, placing in the top 25%. General compute metrics align with median performance across platforms, with stress-ng yielding 1,707.28 single-core and 13,645.62 multi-core scores, and Geekbench scoring 1,876.0 single-core and 9,945.0 multi-core.

Performance tradeoffs appear in specialized compute operations, where the PassMark CPU encryption score of 1,512.38 and LLM token generation tests reflect lower relative efficiency. Lacking bundled local storage, the instance relies entirely on network-attached storage. Given the 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and top-tier memory benchmarks, the x8g.2xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound architectures, including Redis caching tiers, in-memory databases, and large-scale data analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x8g.2xlarge is an arm64 memory-optimized instance engineered for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Powered by 8 dedicated AWS Neoverse-V2 Graviton cores clocked at 2.8 GHz and managed by the Nitro hypervisor, the instance provides 128.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high allocation of 16.0 GB per core. Hardware benchmarks show top-tier memory subsystem throughput, highlighted by a PassMark memory score of 3,139.44 and strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression speeds of 14.47 GB/s. General processing metrics across Geekbench and stress-ng remain in the middle tier, while cryptographic operations and LLM inference tasks show diminished efficiency. The server provides 4 Gbps baseline networking and excludes bundled local storage as well as GPU acceleration. The x8g.2xlarge delivers efficient resource density for in-memory data processing, distributed Redis caching, and memory-bound transactional databases.
